title: On adjoint orbits in nilpotent ideals of a Borel subalgebra: the intersection theorem (Theorem 3.2)
author: Rupert W. T. Yu
work: On adjoint orbits in nilpotent ideals of a Borel subalgebra
difficulty_reason:
Counted unit: the paper's intersection theorem for closed Borel-stable subsets, printed as Theorem 3.2 of the paper (source0.tex lines 330--333), delivered together with the paper's own complete proof of it at source0.tex lines 334--404. The statement is that the intersection of two non empty closed B-stable subsets of m^bullet is non empty, for an arbitrary nilpotent ideal m of the Borel subalgebra b of a complex finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra; it is the theorem that supplies the uniqueness half of the paper's main result (the abstract's unique closed B-orbit in m^bullet), and the paper's own stated main result (printed as Theorem 1.1, source0.tex lines 106--111) carries no proof anywhere in the paper, so the counted unit is the paper's main proved theorem rather than a formal restatement of an unproved one.

The author's proof is complete and is carried out at the level of coordinate rings. After localising the coordinate ring of m at the product phi of the coordinate functions attached to the minimal roots of m, and identifying m^bullet with the non-vanishing locus of phi, the author splits the coordinate ring of m^bullet as the coordinate ring of m_0^bullet plus the kernel of the comorphism of the projection, using the B_0-equivariant projection of m^bullet onto m_0^bullet. Taking a proper B-stable ideal J, the author observes that its image is a B_0-stable ideal in the coordinate ring of m_0^bullet, where the open B_0-orbit of m_0 (Richardson) forces that image to be either zero or the whole ring. In the second case the author uses that the group M_0 with Lie algebra m_0 is unipotent to average an element f of J with f + g equal to the constant 1 along M_0, obtaining non constant elements f-tilde in the m_0-invariants of J and g-tilde in the m_0-invariants of the kernel whose sum is a constant; the weight decomposition in the negative semi-group generated by the minimal roots, together with the proposition proved immediately before the counted theorem (that those invariants reduce to the polynomial ring on the minimal-root coordinates), lets the author multiply g-tilde by a power of phi and land inside that polynomial ring, which is impossible for a non zero element of the kernel. Hence the image of every proper B-stable ideal is zero. The conclusion is the ideal-theoretic form of the statement: two proper B-stable ideals can never sum to the unit ideal, so two non empty closed B-stable subsets of m^bullet must meet.

Carrying this out requires the invariant theory of unipotent group actions, the dense-orbit theorem of Richardson and the theorem of Rosenlicht that the B-invariant rational functions on m_0 are constant, the weight bookkeeping for semi-invariant regular functions with weights in the negative semi-group generated by the minimal roots, the localisation dictionary between the open subset m^bullet and its coordinate ring, and the translation between closed B-stable subsets and B-stable ideals. No qualifying examination poses this: the argument is the technical heart of a research paper on B-orbits in nilpotent ideals, it is stated for an arbitrary nilpotent ideal in an arbitrary type, and the paper's introduction says that no such general statement was available in the literature. That places the unit in the upper qualifying-to-research range: H2.
